R-squared for Mixed Models as Numbers

Source: R/R2_glmm.R
R2_model.Rd

The R-squared of a mixed model as a numeric result. method = "piepho" (the default) gives the same values as R2_glmm (Piepho, 2023), as proportions: total, fixed, random and each random-effect component. method = "nakagawa" gives the marginal (fixed effects) and conditional (fixed and random effects) R-squared of Nakagawa and Schielzeth (2013), with random slopes as Johnson (2014): the variance of each random-effect term is the mean of \(z_i' \Sigma z_i\) over the observations.

Usage

R2_model(model, method = c("piepho", "nakagawa"), over_disp = FALSE)

Arguments

model

A model fitted by lmer, glmer or glmmTMB.

method

"piepho" or "nakagawa".

over_disp

For "piepho": as in R2_glmm.

Value

A named numeric vector of proportions (class "pm_r2", printed as percentages). For "nakagawa", Marginal and Conditional, with attribute "variances": the fixed-effect, random-effect and observation-level variances.

Details

For "nakagawa" the observation-level variance is the residual variance for gaussian models and the variance of the latent distribution for binomial models: \(\pi^2/3\) (logit), 1 (probit) or \(\pi^2/6\) (cloglog). Other families have several competing approximations; use method = "piepho" for them.

References

Piepho, H.-P. (2023), An adjusted coefficient of determination (R2) for generalized linear mixed models in one go, Biometrical Journal, 65(7), 2200290.

Nakagawa, S. and Schielzeth, H. (2013), A general and simple method for obtaining R2 from generalized linear mixed-effects models, Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 4, 133-142.

Johnson, P. C. D. (2014), Extension of Nakagawa & Schielzeth's R2GLMM to random slopes models, Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 5, 944-946.

Author

Dongwen Luo, Siva Ganesh and John Koolaard

Examples

  library(predictmeans)
  fm <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = sleepstudy)
  R2_model(fm)
#> # Adjusted R2 for mixed models (Piepho)
#>        Total        Fixed       Random      Subject Subject.Days 
#>       79.36%       28.02%       51.34%       18.32%       30.43% 
  R2_model(fm, "nakagawa")
#> # R2 for mixed models (Nakagawa and Schielzeth)
#>    Marginal Conditional 
#>      27.87%      79.92%
